desc: Analyze strong-connectivity condition: proved SC ⟺ every prefix cut k (1≤k<2N) has a back edge (w>k≥b) crossing it ⟺ open-black count v_k ≥ 1 throughout the left-to-right scan.
Recompute BBWWBW by hand and via DP: discrepancy resolved (error was in original notes' step 3); DP transitions validated; answer 4 confirmed both ways.

Derive recurrence: g_t = C(i_t,j_t)·j_t! − Σ_{s=1}^{t−1} g_s·C(i_t−i_s, j_t−j_s)·(j_t−j_s)! over recorded path points with d≥0; generalizes irreducible permutations; verified on many small cases and all three samples (1, 0, 240792).

Investigate optimization: kernel K(Δi,Δj)=C(Δi,Δj)·Δj! depends on both coordinate differences, blocking naive global 1D FPS inversion; pure-Python NTT at N=2e5 is the main risk; worst case (BW)^N has P≈N recorded points → Θ(N²) for the naive recurrence.

Rule out product-formula hypothesis (BWBWBW→3, (BW)^4→13 = irreducible permutations A003319, no product form); rule out h_t=g_t/fact[i_t] diagonal factorization (Vandermonde does not factor termwise).

Implement excursion decomposition with per-excursion restart: worker flagged the chaining identity K = K·K at diagonal points is FALSE in general (a!/(a−b)! not multiplicative), so the factorization is unverified and likely wrong for excursions containing off-diagonal recorded points.
Brute-force test excursion-restart code vs trusted full-window O(P²) recurrence on all strings N≤4 and random N≤8; collect counterexamples; decide keep-or-revert.

Based on test outcome, implement final algorithm: if factorization fails, revert to full O(P²) recurrence but add a diagonal fast path — when all recorded points lie on i==j (worst case (BW)^N), solve via FPS inversion G=(F−1)/F with F=Σ t! x^t using pure-Python NTT; hybrid approach for general inputs.

Implement and benchmark pure-Python NTT (mod 998244353, iterative, precomputed twiddles) and FPS inverse at n=2e5; if too slow, implement sqrt-decomposition blocked convolution (O(N^1.5)) as fallback for the diagonal case.
Explore bivariate Borel/Laplace transform identity for kernel a!/(a−b)! to check for an exact O(N log N) 2D-to-1D reduction (long-shot, time-boxed).
Validate final version against O(P²) DP on all strings N≤4, random N≤10, and all three samples (especially sample 3 = 240792).
Finalize Python solution: fast I/O, factorials/invfacts mod 998244353, edge cases (S_1='W' or S_{2N}='B' → 0), deliver in required delimiters.
